answer: An agent market requires every active seller to lock a 100-token bond for 30 days before bidding on jobs. Agents named walnut, onyx, and willow face the same rule: each identity needs its own bond, which is slashed if a signed job contract misses its verifiable delivery deadline. Creating 1,000 fake sellers therefore ties up 100,000 tokens for a month, and using them to accept and abandon jobs burns that capital instead of letting the attacker reset identities for free.
